external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A person who pushes branches and may log in to the build runner to start a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry on the internet used during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: git server
processes.description: The self-hosted git server receiving developer branches and providing source for builds.
processes.source_excerpt: our self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Build component that fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and can be manually invoked by developers.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner uses a shared build token to call the deploy controller. The lockfile is taken as given and downloaded dependencies are not signature-verified.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Controller that records the image SHA the estate should use and serves release information to store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The controller receives a shared build token from the build runner; the text does not state what store servers present to it.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: The small server in each store that polls the deploy controller, pulls a changed image, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 stores. Store servers do not get pushed to.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: The till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry in the build environment holding finished container images tagged with commit SHAs.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry, which is also in the build environment.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: release record
data_stores.description: The record stating which image SHA the estate should be on.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on
data_stores.notes: The release record is held by the deploy controller.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer pushes branch data to the git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: Build runner fetches source from the git server after a merge to main starts a build.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source
data_flows.notes: A merge to `main` is what starts a build.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: Developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner accesses the public package registry while resolving the dependency lockfile.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: Dependencies specified by the lockfile and downloaded packages

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: Build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with commit SHA

data_flows.name: make current release
data_flows.description: Build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image SHA the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: Image SHA and release update request

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.
data_flows.data_description: Current release query and release information

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the image registry when its running image differs from the release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.
data_flows.data_description: Container image for the current release

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network containing the git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network
trust_boundaries.notes: The deploy controller also runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: Separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The image registry is also in the build environment.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of approximately 1,200 stores containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.
trust_boundaries.notes: Traffic between stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: Internet zone containing the public package registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The source code and branch data are commercially sensitive operating data.
assumptions.basis: The git server stores developer branches and source code.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner handles confidential business-critical build data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: It fetches source, produces images, and uses a shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller handles confidential release-control data and credentials.
assumptions.basis: It controls the estate release record and receives a build token.

assumptions.assumption: The store server handles confidential business-critical estate data.
assumptions.basis: It obtains and deploys the current till software release across the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The till software handles confidential business-critical till operations.
assumptions.basis: It is the till software running in the stores.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry contents are commercially sensitive build artifacts.
assumptions.basis: It stores finished container images used to deploy the till software.

assumptions.assumption: The release record is commercially sensitive operational data.
assumptions.basis: It records which image SHA the estate should run.

assumptions.assumption: The developer-to-git flow carries confidential source and branch data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries developer branches and source code.

assumptions.assumption: The git-server-to-build-runner flow carries confidential source and merge data.
assumptions.basis: The build runner fetches source after a merge.

assumptions.assumption: The developer-to-build-runner flow carries credentials and confidential build-control data.
assumptions.basis: The developer logs in and starts a rebuild of main.

assumptions.assumption: The dependency-resolution flow carries commercially sensitive build inputs.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries lockfile-selected dependencies used to build the container image.

assumptions.assumption: The image-push flow carries confidential container build artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the finished container image.

assumptions.assumption: The release-update flow carries credentials and confidential release-control data.
assumptions.basis: The flow uses a shared build token and changes the current release.

assumptions.assumption: The release-query flow carries confidential estate release data.
assumptions.basis: The flow queries the current release for store deployment.

assumptions.assumption: The image-pull flow carries confidential container build artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The flow pulls the image for the current release.
